newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shops shut in Hebron after bombs thrown at troops.
newsitem.headline: Shops shut in Hebron after bombs thrown at troops.

text.p: Israel's army said on Monday it was barring commerce in parts of the volatile West Bank town of Hebron after Palestinian protesters threw bombs at soldiers.
Palestinians said the army was preventing about 150 shops from opening near the dividing line between Israeli- and Palestinian-controlled parts of the town.
The army arrested about 20 Arabs in Hebron late on Sunday after protesters threw several homemade bombs at soldiers, the Palestinians said.
"The army barred this morning the opening of shops and commerce in parts of...Hebron where bombs were thrown last night," an army spokesman said.
A Reuters cameramen said two Israeli soldiers harassed him as he videotaped them detaining a Palestinian in Hebron. He said the soldiers pushed him and threatened to break his camera.
Near Hebron, troops bulldozed a vineyard farmed by Palestinians, witnesses said. They said soldiers told Palestinians the land near Givat Harsina was government-owned.
The army said it was checking the report.

Hebron was the scene of clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops after a right-wing Jewish woman pasted posters on storefronts in the town last month depicting the Moslem prophet Mohammad as a pig.
The violence subsided when Palestinian police intervened two weeks ago but flares up occasionally.

Israel handed over about 80 percent of Hebron -- home to 100,000 Palestinians and 400 Jewish settlers -- to the PLO under peace deals last January but keeps soldiers in the rest of the town to protect Jewish enclaves.
